subject.title: lossless-claw bootstraps into quarantine after every Gateway restart due to new sessionId generating fresh JSONL file

question: Should OpenClaw accept `session.restartContinuation` as the opt-in contract for preserving aborted main-session ids across controlled Gateway restarts, or should the fix wait for a broader restart-recovery design?
rationale: The source-level gap is still present, but the proposed repair adds a compatibility-sensitive session config surface and changes session-state reuse semantics, which repository policy treats as a maintainer product/upgrade decision.

options.title: Sponsor the linked opt-in
options.body: Proceed with reviewing and landing the linked PR if maintainers accept an explicit `session.restartContinuation` knob for this narrow Gateway restart continuity case.

options.title: Require config-free recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open but redirect implementation toward a generic restart-recovery mechanism that avoids another session config option.

options.title: Reject this direction
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not preserve aborted session ids for this LCM workflow.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the linked opt-in
recommendation.body: Proceed with reviewing and landing the linked PR if maintainers accept an explicit `session.restartContinuation` knob for this narrow Gateway restart continuity case.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the terminal-main transcript reconciliation behavior that the proposed fix modifies and have adjacent follow-up work in the same session transcript area.
